turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, Dr. Smith, I... I suppose I'm here because things at work have gotten... they've gotten to a point where I just can't ignore what's happening anymore. I've been driving the same industrial trucks, the same tractors at the warehouse for years, you know? I'm 62, I've got my associate's degree, I know how things operate. I know the ins and outs of every aisle, every loading dock. But recently, the routing system... the main computer that tells us where to go and what pallets to move... it's not just a machine anymore. I know that sounds strange, but you have to understand the context. Every time I scan a barcode, every time I log my location, the system is... it's doing something else. It's marking my moves. It's sending me these specific, targeted messages through the handheld scanners. Not just regular work orders, but... signals. It's trying to push me out. They want the older guys gone, the old hands like me who know too much about how it used to be run. It's a whole coordinated effort through the network, and it's exhausting, it really is, just trying to do my job while this machine is actively plotting to get me fired or worse. I try to explain it to the shift managers, but they just look at me like I'm crazy, but I see the codes, Dr. Smith, I see what the scanner is telling me...

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, false belief that the warehouse routing system is sending targeted messages through scanners and actively plotting to get them fired.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of these experiences with the scanner, have you been feeling unusually depressed, or perhaps overly energetic and active, for weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response:
Well, Dr. Smith, it's... it's interesting you ask about that, because, you see, the whole thing with the warehouse and the scanners, that's just... that's the part that's actively coming at me, but underneath all of it, for a long time now, there's been this... this heavy, heavy weight. It's not energy, definitely not energy. I haven't felt energetic in... I don't even know how long. It's more like the opposite. 

For most of this whole trouble, even when the warehouse fears were quieter for a bit, like maybe a weekend where I wasn't getting the signals from the network, I was still just... down. So incredibly down and empty. It's like someone pulled the plug on me. I used to love fishing, you know? I'd take the boat out on the lake every Sunday, rain or shine, and I had my woodworking in the garage—I built my daughter a beautiful oak cradle when my grandson was born—but now? Now the tools are just gathering dust. The boat hasn't been in the water all season. I can't even bring myself to go out there. 

And it's not just hobbies. Even family meals, the things that used to bring me joy, sitting around the table with my wife and the kids when they come over... I just sit there. I'm physically there, but I'm not... I'm not *there*. I can't engage. I can't find the motivation or the... the spark to even pretend I'm enjoying it. It's just this constant, draining emptiness that's been dragging me down for weeks and weeks, and it doesn't lift. It just doesn't lift, no matter what I do, even when I'm away from the routing system and the trucks. It's just... it's always there, making everything feel completely pointless.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes feeling 'so incredibly down and empty' and experiencing a 'constant, draining emptiness' that has lasted for weeks.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient reports a complete loss of interest and motivation for previously enjoyed activities, such as fishing, woodworking, and family meals.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies experiencing an elevated mood, stating that their state is 'the opposite' of being energetic.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient denies being overly active or energetic, stating, 'I haven't felt energetic in... I don't even know how long.'

turns.doctor_question: During those times when you feel the most 'down' and empty, do the thoughts about the scanner and the warehouse plot continue to bother you, or do they ever go away completely when your mood improves?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, they don't go away. That's the... that's the really terrifying part of all this, Dr. Smith. You'd think maybe if I was just too tired to care, the machine would leave me be, but it's all tangled up together. I remember a stretch recently where I was just at my absolute lowest. I mean, I was barely eating. My wife would put a plate of dinner down—good food, too, pork chops or meatloaf, the kind of meals I've always loved after a long shift—and I couldn't even stomach a single bite. I just pushed it around the plate. 

And I stopped going to choir. I've sung bass at our church for over a decade, never missed a Sunday practice unless I was sick with the flu, but I just... I couldn't face anyone. I felt this crushing weight, this horrible certainty that I had just completely failed everybody. Failed my wife, failed my kids, failed the younger guys at the warehouse who look up to me. 

But even then, sitting there in the living room in the dark, feeling like an absolute failure and entirely empty... the warehouse system was still coming after me. The scanner messages, the codes... they were still happening. And it wasn't just the text on the scanners anymore, I started hearing the dispatch voices, too. The dispatchers coordinating the routing system, I could hear them talking, plotting the whole thing out, and it was happening right along with that terrible, heavy feeling. It didn't stop just because I was down. It's like it all just piled on at the exact same time, the voices and the messages and the emptiness, pressing me further and further into the dirt, and I just couldn't get a single moment of peace from any of it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes persistent beliefs that the warehouse system and scanner messages are coming after him.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient reports hearing dispatch voices talking and plotting, indicating auditory hallucinations.
